_meta.engine: TTREngine64.exe (Toontown Rewritten), Windows x86-64, embedded CPython 3.8.17, packed + symbol-stripped (12 exports, none CPython)
_meta.derivation: OUT-OF-PROCESS ReadProcessMemory dump of the UNPACKED image (the on-disk PE is packed: .tdata is 20MB virtual / 0 raw, entropy ~7.98, no plaintext strings). Symbols located by (a) the x64 exception directory .pdata giving exact bounds for 92035 functions, (b) unique error-string RIP-relative xrefs, (c) PyErr_BadInternalCall (__FILE__,__LINE__) pairs matched against real CPython 3.8.17 source -- the same disambiguator capi-symbols2.md used on arm64, (d) capstone disassembly to CONFIRM semantics. Every addr below was read, not inferred.
_meta.cross_validation: tuple line numbers (New=85, Size=142, GetItem=153, SetItem=169) match capi-symbols2.md's arm64 values exactly; struct offsets (tp_call+0x80, tp_getattr+0x40, tp_setattr+0x48, tp_vectorcall_offset+0x38, tp_flags vectorcall byte@+0xa9 bit3, ml_flags@+0x10 mask 0x8F, PyThreadState.recursion_depth+0x20) all confirmed identical to the arm64 notes.
_meta.float_construction: PyFloat_FromDouble exists OUT-OF-LINE here, so the agent calls it directly instead of the hand-built makeFloat recipe the arm64 build needs. That removes the need for FLOAT_FREELIST / FLOAT_NUMFREE / PYMALLOC_FN / PYMALLOC_CTX entirely -- and with them the only WRITE targets, so we no longer poke CPython's allocator bookkeeping ourselves. Recorded for reference: freelist head 0x141fc3838, numfree 0x141fc3840.
_meta.status: Complete for the injector's NEED list + tuple builder + hook site + float construction. NEVER validated against a live client -- the first attach is still unproven.
_meta.bootstrap: Interceptor.attach on engine code FAIL-FASTS this client (0xc0000409 at ntdll+0xa1a21, the same guard that fires on a bulk read of the packed region). PyGILState_Ensure/Release let a frida thread take the GIL and run the install directly, patching nothing. The Interceptor hook was only ever a bootstrap to reach a GIL-held moment -- the mod itself (a PyCFunction trampoline setattr'd onto the interval class) is pure C-API and patches no code, so it is unaffected.
_meta.signature_scan: scanBySignature (which resolves LocalToon, and therefore BOTH tunnel mechanisms) bails immediately unless GetIter+IterNext+AsUTF8+DictGetStr+DictGetItem+GetAttrStr are ALL bound. Missing PyObject_GetIter/PyIter_Next made it return [] silently, so no class ever matched any signature. MetaInterval resolved only because it uses the hardcoded override path, not the scan.
